number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged under Sections 498-A, 34 IPC and 4 Dowry Prohibition Act, but the FIR was quashed qua the appellants
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the FIR was an abuse of the process of the court, noting that Respondent No.2 resided for less than three weeks in the matrimonial home, lived with her husband in Hyderabad and then moved to London and Sweden, and that the husband of Respondent No.2 had emailed a complaint to the Superintendent of Police three days prior to the wife lodging her complaint.
witness_credibility: The court found the allegations against the appellants to be far-fetched and not to inspire confidence, indicating that the credibility of the main witnesses (Respondent No.2) was questioned.
bail_history: Anticipatory bail granted to the appellants by the learned Sessions Judge, Gwalior dated 26.11.2018

trial_duration.high_court_decision: Impugned Judgment dated 30.04.2019 dismissed the petition for quashing FIR
trial_duration.supreme_court_decision: Appeal allowed, FIR quashed qua the appellants

legal_representation.accused: Ms. Vibha Datta Makhija, Sr. Adv., Karan Mamgain, Praveen Gaur, Ms. Banni Khanna, Vikrant Singh Bais, Yogesh Tiwari, Ms. Neema
legal_representation.state: Gopal Jha, Akshay Sahay, Rohil Bansal, Lzafeer Ahmad B. F.

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.high_court: Impugned Judgment dated 30.04.2019 dismissed the petition for quashing FIR
appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeal allowed, FIR quashed qua the appellants

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the allegations against the appellants were substantiated and that the FIR did not constitute an abuse of the process of the court, citing precedents where the veracity of allegations could not be tested at the investigation stage and that the allegations of cruelty and harassment were credible.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR was an abuse of the process of the court, as the complainant had not resided in the matrimonial home for a significant period, had moved to Sweden, and the criminal case was a retaliatory tactic. They also highlighted discrepancies in the complainant's statements and the timing of the complaint, suggesting it was an afterthought.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the FIR should be quashed if it is an abuse of the process of the court, and that the allegations must be examined for their credibility and whether they constitute a genuine case or a misuse of legal processes.
precedent_relied_upon: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam v State of Bihar (2022) 6 SCC 599; Rajesh Sharma v State of Uttar Pradesh (2018) 10 SCC 472; State of Haryana v Bhajan Lal 1992 Suppl. (1) SCC 335; Pawan Kumar v State of Haryana (1998) 3 SCC 309; Mahendra K C v State of Karnataka (2022) 2 SCC 129; Central Bureau of Investigation v A Ravishankar Prasad (2009) 6 SCC 351; S Mahaboob Basha v State of Karnataka (2014) 10 SCC 244; Rupali Devi v State of Uttar Pradesh (2019) 5 SCC 384
